newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks strong but Greenspan jitters grow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks strong but Greenspan jitters grow.

text.p: European stocks were strong on Tuesday, despite a lacklustre opening on Wall Street, although worries emerged about what U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will tell Congress this week.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar stabilised after easing from early highs against the mark, with some analysts confident that it would continue to reflect the fact that the U.S. economy is stronger than Germany's.

French and German stocks led the way with both markets up 1.5 percent, even though Wall Street got off to a slow start with the Dow Jones Industrial Average bouncing around Monday's closing level in the first hour of trade.
In Frankfurt, the DAX Index closed up 49.0 points at 3,233.21 while by mid afternoon the Paris CAC-40 index was 38.34 points higher at 2,607.19.
Dealers said the European markets were reacting not to Tuesday's Dow but its Monday perfomance when it jumped 1.1 percent to 7,008.20 due to a strong U.S. economy, a firm dollar and low inflation.
"This is really the follow-through from Wall Street yesterday," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The Street isn't really doing that much today, but a lot of stocks seem better on sentiment."
A firm dollar against the mark, which helps German exporters, plus a strong debt market helped to support stocks.
London was up a more modest 0.48 percent, with the FTSE 100 index 21.0 points higher at 4,352.1 at mid afternoon, albeit only 10 points below its record high.

Earlier in the day, European investors seemed to have set aside their traditional wariness before the Fed chairman Greenspan speaks. But with the Dow down marginally after the first hour of trade, the tide of opinion began to turn.

By mid afternoon investors started to show signs of nervousness before the central bank chief delivers his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins report on the state of the U.S. economy to Congress this week and next.
Last autumn Greenspan caught investors off guard when he wiped billions of dollars off share prices worldwide by warning them of "irrational exuberance" on the markets.
Since then, Greenspan has delivered a gentler assessment of the markets, and interest rates have remained stable as the U.S. economy has achieved steady growth with low inflation.

Analysts expect him to give a positive report when he testifies to the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT on Wednesday and to a House Banking subcommittee on March 5. But he may include some words of caution about the course of inflation and possibly the stock market.

The dollar was at 1.6753 marks, off its high but above its late European level of 1.6700 on Monday. Against the yen, it reversed earlier slippage to 121.99, little changed from its late Monday level of 122.05.
Some analysts said the dollar's energy was flagging, but this suggested the market was waiting for cues on which way to go, and the slowness did not necessarily herald a downturn.

"In general we need more information, either to confirm a dollar topping scenario or to send the dollar up against the mark and yen," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London.

But some analysts said economic fundamentals would hold sway. Recent German data which were slightly better than expectations were not enough to shake the general perception of a strong U.S. economy and weakness in Germany's.

"Data in the weeks and months ahead will probably show a bit of a weakening in the U.S. economy and probably show an improvement in Germany," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International in London.
"But in terms of absolute rates of growth, we'll still see relative strength in the U.S. rather than in Germany."
Elsewhere, the Italian government won a parliamentary confidence vote as expected but the lira slipped to 994.50 to the mark from 992.55 at the opening.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6753 marks and 121.99 yen, compared with 1.6700 and 122.05 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 21.0 points at 4,352.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 rose 39.34 points to 2,607.19.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 49.0 points at 3,233.21.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $353.10 an ounce compared with the $353.45 morning fix. Silver was down three cents at $5.19.
